messages:
Maya: acme-corp reporting 502 spike from hosted inference since ~09:10 UTC. Edge logs show TLS handshake timeouts. Sample:
```
[09:11:02.234] gw=eu-west-1 connection_id=0x7f3f tls_handshake_timeout client_ip=198.51.100.44 sni=api.acme.example
[09:11:02.235] gw=eu-west-1 connection_id=0x7f3f closing after timeout
```
No app errors. customer seeing retries. Any quick checks? :thinking:

Evan: Are requests hitting same backend IPs? Any pattern w/ SNI or Host header? Can you grab a tcpdump?

Maya: Attached tcpdump snippet (trimmed):
```
09:10:58.123 IP 198.51.100.44.52345 > 10.0.5.12.443: Flags [S]
09:10:58.223 IP 10.0.5.12.443 > 198.51.100.44.52345: Flags [R]
09:11:02.124 IP 198.51.100.44.52346 > 10.0.5.12.443: Flags [S]
# repeated SYNs then no handshake
```
In some traces server sends RST quickly, other times SYNs retry then TLS timeout.

Samir: RST from 10.0.5.12 looks like an active reject. Could be wrong backend IP (old host without cert) or firewall. Any DNS diffs? Run dig from edge node and from resolver used by node.

Jamie: I just ran quick checks: dig +short api.acme.example from two nodes: NodeA -> 10.0.5.12; NodeB -> 10.0.5.55. But node resolver results differ when querying our internal resolver vs upstream. Also saw EDNS0 UDP truncation on some queries (-> TCP fallback sporadic). Paste dig output:
```
; nodeA -> internal-resolver
api.acme.example. 30 IN A 10.0.5.12
; nodeB -> public-resolver
api.acme.example. 30 IN A 10.0.5.55
```

InfraBot: DNS rollout for acme-corp A records started at 09:05 UTC (change to LB pool). Propagation expected 60s, but some caches honor longer TTLs.

DeployBot: We rotated certs for backend pool B at 09:06 UTC (new cert on 10.0.5.55). Old pool (10.0.5.12) still has previous cert which was removed from rotation but returned in DNS for some resolvers.

Samir: That explains RSTs: some edge nodes resolved to the decommissioned IP without a valid cert, the backend kernel or LB actively RSTs. Correlation between DNS cache mismatch and cert rotation.

Evan: Action plan: 1) ask customer to pause traffic briefly (or we reroute) 2) flush edge node resolver caches (systemd-resolved/ndc) 3) re-add old cert or ensure old backend returns a proper 443 teardown (graceful), 4) monitor 502 rate.

Maya: Flushed caches on affected EU nodes and temporarily readded cert to 10.0.5.12. Customer reports errors drop to baseline within ~45s. :tada: 

Jamie: Followup: add guard in deploy flow to hold DNS switch until cert rotation fully synced across route table and invalidate edge caches via API. Filed a ticket: infra-ops#4521.

Maya: Customer confirmed recovery, will keep watch. Thanks all.

Evan: Recommend we add a postmortem blurb to the next infra change doc and add DNS-checks to rollout checklist. :+1:
